slides.title: PanoTac: A Dense Three-Axis Tactile Sensor for Robust Touch-Centric Manipulation
slides.highlight: PanoTac offers a low-cost, compliant tactile fingertip providing dense three-axis sensing (normal and shear forces) at 60 Hz. Integrated into a visuo-tactile pipeline, it significantly outperforms vision-only baselines in contact-rich manipulation tasks like scooping and pouring.

card.one_liner: PanoTac is a low-cost, dense three-axis tactile fingertip that significantly improves robotic manipulation success rates.
card.key_idea: Combines a dense piezoresistive array for normal contact with magnetic sensors for shear, yielding a 12x32x3 tactile representation.
card.evaluation: Tested on three touch-centric tasks; outperformed vision-only baselines by 46.7% and ablations confirmed the necessity of both modalities.
card.limitation: Susceptible to external magnetic interference, limited force resolution due to elastomer compliance, and currently designed for parallel-jaw grippers.

slides.title: ReContact: Reconstruct and Retarget Human Contacts from Video for Contact-Rich Humanoid Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a method to reconstruct and retarget human-object contact plans from video, enabling humanoid robots to perform complex, whole-body manipulation tasks beyond simple grasps. It is relevant to RwB for advancing embodied learning techniques that allow robots to acquire sophisticated physical interaction skills from human demonstrations.

card.one_liner: ReContact reconstructs and retargets human contacts from video for contact-rich humanoid manipulation.
card.key_idea: Uses an object-centric contact plan to guide reconstruction, retargeting, and residual RL rewards for precise contact forces.
card.evaluation: Validated in simulation (83.5% regrasp success) and on a Unitree G1 robot across nine tasks, outperforming baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on GPT-6 Astra for plan drafting, potentially introducing errors in complex or ambiguous contact scenarios.

slides.title: DexHOT: Learning Hand-Object Configuration Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: DexHOT formulates dexterous manipulation as hand-object configuration transfer, providing an explicit interface for joint hand articulation and object pose. This approach aligns with MOSAIC's focus on procedural skill acquisition by enabling reusable, relation-conditioned primitives for complex manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: DexHOT learns hand-object configuration transfer via synthetic feasible pairs, enabling composable dexterous manipulation without human motion references.
card.key_idea: Formulates manipulation as transferring between hand-object configurations using a relation-conditioned RL policy trained on synthetic feasible pairs, composed via hierarchical chaining.
card.evaluation: DexHOTBench (120 objects) shows 80.5% seen/69.4% unseen success; real robot achieves 61.5% transfer and 90% task success, outperforming baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic feasible configuration pools; struggles with low-friction objects and elongated tools due to slippage and tracking loss.

slides.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: The paper introduces ToFTouch, a multimodal sensor combining time-of-flight and pressure sensing to enable anticipatory robotic manipulation, demonstrating reduced cycle times and improved precision in pre-grasp adjustments and cluttered environments.

card.one_liner: ToFTouch combines multizone ToF proximity and tactile sensing to enable anticipatory robotic manipulation in cluttered environments.
card.key_idea: Integrates three 4x4 multizone ToF sensors with an optics-based tactile array on a compact gripper fingertip for pre-contact and contact feedback.
card.evaluation: Tested on pre-grasp, extraction, and insertion tasks; showed 7.4% cycle time reduction and robust depth correction across ±2cm offsets.
card.limitation: Limited trial counts, lack of statistical rigor, sensor overheating issues, and uncalibrated depth discrepancies affect reliability.

slides.title: Visuo-tactile Diffusion Policy for Robotic Manipulation with Auxiliary Tactile Dynamics Prediction
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a visuo-tactile diffusion policy that integrates multi-view camera data and fingertip tactile images with an auxiliary tactile dynamics prediction objective, significantly improving success rates in long-horizon robotic assembly tasks.

card.one_liner: Visuo-tactile diffusion policy improves robotic assembly success by predicting future tactile changes during training.
card.key_idea: Combines visual and tactile histories via recurrent representation; auxiliary loss predicts future tactile changes to enhance contact understanding.
card.evaluation: MuJoCo assembly tasks; 59.0% success vs 42.7% visual-only baseline; validated across three training seeds.
card.limitation: Evaluated only in simulated MuJoCo environments; real-world generalization and hardware transferability remain unverified.

slides.title: Should the Action Expert Train the VLM? Action-Token Supervision and Gradient Routing in Mixture-of-Transformer VLAs
slides.tldr: Gradient insulation in VLAs is not always optimal
slides.highlight: This study challenges the default practice of blocking gradients from action experts to vision-language models in VLA architectures, showing that the benefit of insulation depends heavily on action-token supervision and evaluation settings.

card.one_liner: Gradient coupling outperforms insulation when action-token supervision is absent, challenging default VLA training recipes.
card.key_idea: Disentangles expert-to-VLM gradient routing from discrete action-token supervision to determine which signal effectively adapts VLM representations for control.
card.evaluation: Tested in autonomous driving and manipulation via open/closed-loop metrics; coupling improved performance significantly without action tokens.
card.limitation: Limited architectural diversity, simulation-only results, single training run per condition, and lack of mechanistic explanation for observed effects.

slides.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
slides.highlight: This work introduces an asynchronous framework that decouples high-level semantic reasoning from low-level action generation, resolving the latency bottleneck in large Vision-Language-Action models. By allowing independent operating frequencies, it achieves significant gains in success rates and execution speed for real-time robot manipulation.

card.one_liner: Decouples VLM reasoning from action generation to enable real-time robot control without latency penalties.
card.key_idea: Asynchronous architecture where a slow VLM updates semantic memory while a fast vision-action expert generates high-frequency control commands.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO, DROID, and Franka robots; shows 18% higher success and 3-5x better dynamic reactivity than synchronous VLAs.
card.limitation: Requires complex training with temporally mismatched data to handle semantic memory staleness and execution delays.

slides.title: Physical Diffusion Policy via MPM-Guided 3D Gaussian Simulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a physics-aware diffusion policy that integrates material property estimation via 3D Gaussian Splatting and Material Point Method simulation, enhancing manipulation generalization across diverse physical regimes.

card.one_liner: Physics-aware diffusion policy using MPM-3DGS simulation to estimate material properties for robust manipulation.
card.key_idea: Couples 3D Gaussian Splatting with differentiable MPM to recover physical parameters, conditioning a material-aware MoE diffusion policy.
card.evaluation: Tested on Isaac Lab and real-world tasks (pick-and-place, stacking) against DP/DP3 baselines, showing improved success rates.
card.limitation: Relies on a physics memory bank for efficient inference, potentially limiting generalization to unseen objects without online optimization.
